extraction.notes: Read in full (nine pages; page 9 is references). Whole document concerns foreign workers in the Western Balkans, so items are Chapter 2 where they concern access to the labour market and rights of foreign workers. Under the rule for regional documents, extracted: claims naming North Macedonia and regional claims in the same section of findings. The Roadmap (pages 7-8) does not name North Macedonia. Its six items (0024 to 0029) were removed at the second pass under the rule for regional documents; their IDs stay unused and their full text is in review/RUN-2026-01/second_pass/MKD-IO-2026-001.csv for the analyst at G5. The highest ID ever used is 0029, so any new item must start at 0030. LEFT OUT as not naming North Macedonia: the recruitment findings on page 5 (unlicensed brokers, debt, monitoring of licensed agencies), which name other countries; claims about emigration from the region (page 2, out under the Chapter 2 boundary); country examples for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro and Serbia. Table 1 (page 4) rows that restate the running text are not extracted again, apart from row 5, which adds a claim (EU alignment, database access). This is a policy summary; the full PSIMM report is not in the source set. Second-pass check done (G3 condition 2). Items removed at the second pass restored at G5 (G5-D02) and marked as regional.

items.stated_text: The Roadmap proposes: extending existing approaches by replacing administratively-set quotas with planning grounded in integrated labour market data, introducing shortage occupation lists as an alternative or complement to rigid quota systems: establishing formal processes for sectoral labour market analysis, with clearly defined roles and regular review cycles; incorporating outbound mobility trends into planning.
items.summary: Replace administrative quotas with data-based planning, introduce shortage occupation lists, set up formal sectoral labour market analysis, and include outbound mobility in planning.

speaker.name_as_stated: International Centre for Migration Policy Development

items.stated_text: The Roadmap proposes: minimum due diligence requirements for employers and intermediaries before they can participate in recruitment; strengthening pre-licensing and periodic inspections and ongoing monitoring of private employment agencies, moving beyond administrative compliance towards substantive assessment of recruitment practices;  establishing registers of sanctioned or non-compliant actors to enable risk-based targeting; introducing trusted-actor frameworks for accredited employers and agencies with strong compliance records to streamline procedures for those who meet ethical standards;  clarifying of the legal status of agencies registered abroad that currently fall entirely outside domestic oversight.
items.summary: Set due diligence for recruiters, strengthen agency inspection and monitoring, register sanctioned actors, create trusted-actor frameworks, clarify the status of agencies registered abroad.

items.stated_text: The Roadmap proposes: introducing a unique foreign worker identifier linking permit records, employment status, social insurance registration, and inspection findings across institutions; establishing structured mandatory reporting of employment commencement and termination; creating regulated pathways for workers to change employers without losing legal status; using risk-based inspections to identify permit non-activation and early contract termination patterns systematically rather than reactively.
items.summary: Introduce a unique foreign worker identifier linking records across institutions, mandatory employment reporting, regulated employer change without losing status, and risk-based inspections.

items.stated_text: The Roadmap proposes: mapping and formalising handover points between institutions at each stage of the migration pathway, including tax authorities, social insurance bodies, and business registries within operational coordination frameworks; introducing routine coordination mechanisms linking frontline implementation with policy decision-making; establishing data governance frameworks defining accesses to information, purpose, and accountability mechanisms.
items.summary: Formalise institutional handover points, add routine coordination mechanisms, and establish data governance frameworks defining access, purpose and accountability.

items.stated_text: The Roadmap proposes: providing workers upon arrival with rights and obligations information in accessible language and format upon arrival; connecting complaint mechanisms to social protection and anti-trafficking referral pathways; introducing clear, confidential complaint channels with guaranteed non-retaliation; providing employers with sector-specific guidance on legal obligations, connecting non-compliance to graduated, proportionate follow-up rather than enforcement-only responses.
